events.title: Jamestown Is Founded
events.description: English colonists led by Edward Maria Wingfield, Christopher Newport and John Smith established a settlement on the James River in Virginia. It became the first permanent English settlement in North America.
events.significance: Jamestown was the starting point for English colonization of North America. It shaped the early history of the United States.

events.title: Jenner Tests the First Smallpox Vaccine
events.description: English physician Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox material. He wanted to test whether it would protect against smallpox.
events.significance: This experiment is regarded as the beginning of vaccination. It eventually led to the worldwide eradication of smallpox.

events.title: Lewis and Clark Set Out
events.description: The Corps of Discovery, led by Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, left Camp Dubois near present-day Hartford, Illinois. Their journey up the Missouri River began the first overland expedition to the Pacific coast and back.
events.significance: The expedition mapped new territory and documented its peoples and wildlife. It encouraged American westward expansion.

events.title: Israel Declares Independence
events.description: David Ben-Gurion announced the establishment of the State of Israel as British rule in Palestine ended. A war with neighboring Arab states began soon afterward.
events.significance: The declaration created a new nation and reshaped the politics of the Middle East.

events.title: Skylab Launches
events.description: The United States launched Skylab, its first space station, into orbit.
events.significance: Skylab hosted three crews and showed that people could live and work in space for long periods. It paved the way for later space stations.
